$schema: Printer catalog for Printer Tycoon. Specs reflect manufacturer claims circa 2024-2026, corrected against the 2026-10-27 realism audit (sources in the round-sim report). baseReliability is the chance a clean, unworn machine finishes a 4-hour job, calibrated to real ranges (Formlabs independent test for resin; audit estimate for FDM). Refresh annually.

fields.tech: FDM | MSLA | SLA | SLS | MJF | DMLS | ADAM
fields.kinematics: how the machine moves (drawing only, never the rules): bedslinger (bed in Y, head in X, gantry climbs in Z) | cantilever (the same, X arm held from one column) | corexy (head in X and Y at the top, bed drops in Z) | idex (two heads on one X beam) | vat (resin plate climbs out of a vat, prints hang upside down) | powder (piston lowers a powder bed under a recoater and a laser or fusing lamp) | metal (bound-metal FFF with wash and sintering stations)
fields.zAxis: corexy only, optional: gantry = the bed stays put and the whole XY gantry climbs (Voron 2.4)
fields.tier: garage | hobbyist | studio | pro | industrial | endgame
fields.maxSpeedMMs: FDM head speed in mm/s; null for non-FDM
fields.throughputGPH: grams per hour of PLA through a 0.4 mm brass nozzle; FDM/FFF/ADAM print time = grams / (throughputGPH x nozzle flow x material speedFactor)
fields.throughputCM3PH: legacy (v4); not used. Vat and powder machines print by height: see verticalMMPerHour
fields.verticalMMPerHour: vat and powder machines: build height per hour with standard material (makers' rated speeds, derated for standard resin); a full plate takes as long as one part
fields.materials: list of material ids that can run on this machine
fields.enclosed: true if the machine has its own closed chamber (an Enclosure kit can be added to open frames)
fields.chamberC: actively heated chamber temperature in C, or null (passive or open)
fields.multiMaterialColors: 0 = single, N = simultaneous colors/materials (AMS, MMU, toolheads)
fields.stockNozzle: nozzle fitted at the factory (FDM/FFF/ADAM): b04 brass, s04 stainless, h04 hardened steel
fields.failureDetection: true if the machine spots a failed print by itself (AI camera, lidar, industrial monitoring)
fields.baseReliability: 0..1 chance a clean, unworn machine finishes a 4-hour job (longer jobs, worn beds, damp spools, warping and worn nozzles all lower it)
fields.precision: 0..1 quality score multiplier on completed prints
fields.powerW: average draw in W while printing PLA-class material (Bambu wiki measurements where marked, else estimates); electricity = W x hours x $0.17/kWh
fields.powerHotW: average draw with ABS/ASA/PC/PA-class material (hot bed and chamber); missing = same as powerW
fields.powerMaxW: power-supply rating (the old powerW values); display only
fields.powerNote: where the average draw comes from
fields.skillRequired: 0 = plug and play, 1.0 = expert build/maintenance required
fields.footprintMM: [w, d] desk/floor footprint for workshop placement

printers.powerNote: estimate (a comparable bed-slinger, the Bambu A1, measures 95 W on PLA)
printers.notes: The cheapest serious starter. Auto-leveling (CR Touch) and a direct-drive Sprite extruder, so TPU works. Open frame: PLA, PETG and TPU in practice.
Direct competitor to Ender 3 series. Slightly worse out of the box, very tunable.
Klipper firmware on a budget machine. Genuinely fast. ABS technically possible but warps without enclosure.
Larger build volume than typical entry. All-metal hot end, direct drive. Rated 150 mm/s (the 500 mm/s figure is the later SV06 Plus ACE). The sleeper pick for hobbyists.

printers.powerNote: Bambu Lab wiki power table (measured, fetched 2026-10-27): 80 W PLA, 75 W PETG
printers.notes: Tiny build volume but appliance-grade reliability. $299 is the single-color printer; the AMS lite combo adds 4 colors. Best in class for new players.

printers.powerNote: Bambu Lab wiki power table (measured, fetched 2026-10-27): 95 W PLA, 200 W ABS
printers.notes: Bigger A1. Open frame still gates ABS/ASA. The natural step up before going enclosed.
Fast, enclosed CoreXY at a low price. Reliability lags Bambu but materials range is broader for the money.

printers.powerNote: typical draw (audit): about 80 W PLA, 120 W ABS; 240 W is the PSU
printers.notes: Slower than CoreXY rivals but legendary reliability. Ships with a brass nozzle: fit hardened steel for carbon fibre. $999 assembled after Prusa's permanent price cut. Add-on enclosure unlocks ABS/ASA/PC properly.

printers.powerNote: Bambu Lab wiki power table (measured, fetched 2026-10-27): 105 W PLA, 140 W ABS, 135 W PC
printers.notes: Sweet spot of the lineup for production. Enclosed for engineering plastics, AMS for color, fast enough to make money. Ships with a stainless 0.4 nozzle; Bambu asks for hardened steel for carbon fibre.

Heated chamber to 65C for ABS, ASA, PC and nylon. Not PEEK: that needs a ~400C nozzle and a 90C chamber. Stock nozzle uncertain (QIDI lists a copper-alloy hot end with hardened steel optional; a review says both are in the box), kept as hardened.

printers.powerNote: Bambu Lab wiki power table (measured, fetched 2026-10-27): 105 W PLA, 150 W ABS, 135 W PC
printers.notes: Lidar first-layer scan, AI failure detection, hardened nozzle for carbon fiber. The workhorse most print farms run. Production ended 2026-03-31 (parts until 2031).

printers.powerNote: Bambu Lab wiki power table (measured, fetched 2026-10-27): 185 W PLA, 260 W ABS, 230 W PC
printers.notes: Industrial X1C variant: 60C heated chamber, ethernet, MAC-locked filament profiles. Engineering and aerospace contracts unlock here. 320C nozzle and 60C chamber: not enough for PEEK.

printers.powerNote: Bambu Lab wiki power table (measured, fetched 2026-10-27): 197 W PLA, 150 W PETG, 395 W PC
printers.notes: Dual nozzle: two materials at $1,899 (the AMS combo adds more). 325 x 320 x 325 mm with one nozzle (350 mm is the combined reach). Fewer purges than one nozzle, not zero. Optional laser/cutting/pen tools turn it into a craft platform.
True 5-tool multi-material with no purge waste. CoreXY motion. The big-build solution for the small shop. Stock nozzle unconfirmed (probably brass), kept as hardened.

printers.powerNote: estimate (the 750 W AC bed drives the peak)
printers.notes: Open-source DIY. Parts cost shown (uncertain: kits run about $1,050-1,600); you supply 40+ hours and significant skill. Hot ends top out near 300C, so no PEEK. Stock nozzle unconfirmed, kept as hardened.

IDEX (independent dual extruder): both heads print at once only in Duplication or Mirror mode (two copies); for two materials one head parks while the other prints. 2.85 mm filament, 300C nozzle, 80C bed, so ABS/ASA/PC/PA are marginal. Stock nozzle unconfirmed, kept as hardened.
Cheap entry into resin. 4K mono LCD, 70 mm/h at most with fast resin, auto-levels with a mechanical sensor. Tiny build volume. Adds post-processing labor (wash + cure).
12K resolution, levelling-free. Averages about 105 mm/h with fast resin (slower with standard). Good for batched miniatures. Since replaced by the M7 Pro.
12K, tilt vat, auto-levels with a mechanical sensor, rated up to 150 mm/h with fast resin. No resin heater. Workhorse for a miniature side hustle. Castable resin opens the jewelry market.
Long history with miniature painters. Reliable when tuned but no auto-leveling.

Low Force Stereolithography: about 40 mm/h on average at 100 um (100 mm/h at most). Closed material ecosystem (cartridges) but proven for dental, jewelry, end-use parts. Price uncertain (launched at $4,500; one retailer lists $3,499).

Continuous fiber reinforcement: lays real strands of carbon fiber inside nylon parts. End-use functional parts at metal-like strength. Built for Onyx (chopped carbon) out of the box; the fibers run through their own fiber nozzle.

Powder-bed SLS, no support structures. $24,649 is the printer with its build chamber (120 V); the Fuse Sift is sold separately (the Complete Package with it is $57,617). 110 um layers. Production-grade nylon parts.

Bound metal deposition + sintering furnace. The printer is about $99,500; Markforged's $124,990 bundle adds the Wash-1 ($9,990) and Sinter-1 ($14,990). Washing alone takes 12-72 h, then sintering. 17% shrinkage on sintering is compensated (parts are printed about 20% oversize). Print rate is an estimate.

printers.powerNote: estimate: HP lists the printer at about 12 kW
printers.notes: True production volume. Up to 4,010 cm3/h of swept build volume (about 37 mm/h over the 380 x 284 mm bed). Needs a processing station (about $78,000) and a cooling unit. No official printer price (estimates $350k-500k+). Service contract effectively required.

printers.powerNote: EOS M 290 data sheet: average 2.4 kW, up to 3.2 kW with platform heating, 8.5 kW maximum
printers.notes: Industry-standard direct metal laser sintering. Aerospace and medical certifications possible. Inert gas (argon/nitrogen) consumable. The endgame contract unlocker.
